name: Iodine (I)
summary: An essential component of thyroid hormones (T3, T4), which set basal metabolic rate and are critical for fetal and infant brain development.

conditions.label: Deficiency
conditions.description: Limits thyroid hormone synthesis, causing goitre and hypothyroidism; the leading preventable cause of intellectual disability worldwide.

affects.detail: Low iodine reduces thyroid hormone output; rising TSH stimulates the gland to enlarge into a visible goitre.

affects.effect: Impaired neurodevelopment (cretinism in severe fetal deficiency)
affects.detail: Thyroid hormone is essential for fetal and infant brain development; severe deficiency causes irreversible intellectual disability.

ageModifiers.infant: Congenital/severe deficiency causes cretinism: intellectual disability, deaf-mutism and stunted growth.
ageModifiers.adult: Hypothyroidism: fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, slowed cognition and depression.

genderModifiers.female: Iodine requirements rise in pregnancy and lactation; maternal deficiency harms fetal brain development.

affects.detail: Reduced thyroid hormone slows heart rate and overall metabolism.
